name: CoreWeave
subsector: GPU cloud and AI data centers
product: A purpose-built cloud for GPU-intensive AI training, inference and related managed services.
targetCustomer: AI labs and enterprises operating large GPU workloads
buyer: CTO, VP Infrastructure, Head of AI Platform
fundingDisplay: $2B equity (January 2026); approximately $18B debt and equity raised during 2025
traction: CoreWeave reported more than $5B FY2025 revenue and a $66.8B revenue backlog in its 2025 shareholder letter.
notes: Public-company financing is not comparable with venture funding, so no cumulative funding total is assigned. The moat is contracted power, capacity, software operations and customer commitments, but leverage and customer concentration are material risks.

name: Lambda
product: GPU cloud, clusters, workstations and servers for AI training and inference.
targetCustomer: AI developers, research organizations and enterprises
buyer: CTO, VP Infrastructure, Head of AI Research
fundingDisplay: Approximately $2.3B equity publicly reported; at least $1.98B in Series D and E verified directly
traction: Lambda said it served more than 150,000 cloud users and that its systems were used in 97% of top US universities when it rebranded in 2024.
notes: The cumulative total relies on a credible secondary compilation because the company does not publish one consolidated figure. Vertical integration across cloud and systems is distinctive; capital intensity and hyperscaler competition remain severe.

name: Crusoe
subsector: Energy-integrated AI cloud and data centers
product: AI cloud and purpose-built data-center infrastructure developed alongside energy projects.
targetCustomer: AI labs and enterprises requiring large-scale compute
buyer: CTO, VP Infrastructure, Data-center and Capacity leaders
fundingDisplay: At least $2.325B equity across Series C-E; project and debt financing excluded
traction: Crusoe said bookings grew fivefold during the first three quarters of 2025.
notes: The equity total is a defensible lower bound, not lifetime capital. Energy and data-center execution create a harder asset moat than a generic GPU reseller, while making the company exceptionally capital intensive.

name: Nebius
product: A full-stack AI cloud offering GPU compute, managed services and developer tooling from European data centers.
targetCustomer: AI companies, research teams and enterprises
buyer: CTO, CIO, VP Infrastructure
fundingDisplay: $5.45B disclosed equity and convertible notes since December 2024
latestRound: $3.75B concurrent convertible notes and equity, September 2025
traction: Nebius reported 674% year-over-year ARR growth in its Q1 2026 shareholder letter.
notes: This is financing raised by a public group and includes convertibles, not venture funding. Group headcount includes businesses outside core AI cloud. European capacity and sovereignty are differentiators, but utilization and capital efficiency must be watched.

name: Nscale
subsector: AI data centers and GPU cloud
product: Vertically integrated AI infrastructure spanning data centers, GPU compute and managed AI services.
targetCustomer: Hyperscalers, frontier AI companies, governments and enterprises
buyer: CIO, CTO, Capacity and Data-center leaders
fundingDisplay: $3.255B announced equity; Series C includes the previously announced $433M pre-C SAFE
traction: Nscale has announced large AI infrastructure projects in Norway and the United Kingdom and commercial agreements with Microsoft; utilization and revenue were not disclosed.
notes: The total avoids double-counting the $433M pre-C SAFE. Power, project finance and sovereign deployment are the present moat; a differentiated software advantage is not yet publicly demonstrated. LinkedIn size and visible-profile counts are inconsistent.

name: Runpod
subsector: Developer-first GPU cloud and serverless inference
product: On-demand GPU pods and serverless endpoints for training, inference and custom container workloads.
targetCustomer: AI developers, startups and platform teams
buyer: Developer, ML Platform Lead, CTO
traction: Runpod reported one million developers and more than ten billion serverless requests by June 2026; in January it reported $120M ARR.
notes: Developer distribution and ease of use are the strongest signals. Its defensibility depends on scheduler reliability, supply quality and developer workflow lock-in rather than access to commodity GPUs alone; ARR and usage are company-reported.

name: Together AI
subsector: Training and inference cloud for open models
product: A cloud platform for training, fine-tuning and serving open-weight and custom AI models.
targetCustomer: AI-native companies and enterprise AI teams
buyer: CTO, VP AI, ML Platform Lead
traction: The Series C announcement says the platform serves thousands of customers; revenue and utilization were not disclosed.
notes: The cumulative total combines directly verified rounds with a credible funding compilation. Technical depth is high, but training and inference clouds face hyperscaler, model-provider and specialized-serving competition plus heavy capital requirements.

name: Fireworks AI
product: A managed platform and APIs for serving, fine-tuning and composing generative AI models.
targetCustomer: AI product companies and enterprise application teams
buyer: CTO, VP Engineering, ML Platform Lead
fundingDisplay: More than $327M; latest financing included primary and secondary capital
traction: Fireworks reported more than 10,000 organizations, ten trillion tokens served daily and more than $280M annualized revenue in October 2025.
notes: Funding cannot be treated as pure new company cash because Series C included secondary. Performance engineering is credible differentiation, but reported revenue and token metrics are unaudited company claims and model serving remains intensely competitive.

name: Baseten
product: A managed platform for deploying, scaling and optimizing production AI model inference.
targetCustomer: AI-native companies and enterprise ML teams
buyer: CTO, VP Engineering, Head of ML Platform
fundingDisplay: Approximately $2.085B publicly reported through Series F
traction: Baseten reported 20-fold revenue growth and 40-fold inference-volume growth during the year before its June 2026 Series F.
notes: The cumulative total adds the $1.5B Series F to the previously reported $585M total. Growth metrics are company-reported. The wedge is inference performance and reliability; durable differentiation must outpace hyperscalers and open-source serving stacks.

name: Modal
hq: New York, New York, United States
product: A Python-first serverless platform providing GPU and CPU compute, containers, storage and secure sandboxes.
targetCustomer: AI developers and engineering teams
buyer: Developer, CTO, VP Engineering
traction: Modal reported more than $300M annualized revenue and fivefold growth since September 2025 in its Series C announcement.
notes: Funding is derived from the prior $111M total plus the $355M Series C. The compact Python developer experience and internally operated compute stack are differentiated; annualized revenue is company-reported and the category is capital intensive.

name: Anyscale
product: A managed compute platform built around the open-source Ray distributed computing framework.
targetCustomer: Enterprise AI and ML platform teams
buyer: CTO, VP AI Infrastructure, ML Platform Lead
traction: Ray is broadly adopted as an open-source distributed AI framework, but current Anyscale revenue and paying-customer counts are not publicly disclosed.
notes: Ray gives Anyscale unusually strong technical distribution and ecosystem leverage. The long interval since disclosed financing and lack of current commercial metrics make conversion from open-source adoption to durable platform economics an important unknown.

name: Replicate
product: An API platform and catalog for running public or private machine-learning models in containers.
targetCustomer: Software developers and AI application teams
buyer: Developer, Engineering Lead, CTO
traction: Replicate reported two million sign-ups and 30,000 paying customers in its 2023 Series B announcement; no current comparable metric was found.
notes: The low-friction API and model catalog are a useful wedge, but funding and traction disclosures are stale and competition from model hosts, inference platforms and direct APIs is intense. Marketplace network effects remain plausible rather than proven.

name: Prime Intellect
product: A platform combining distributed GPU supply, reinforcement-learning infrastructure, evaluations, sandboxes and inference.
targetCustomer: AI researchers, model builders and AI-native companies
buyer: Research Lead, CTO, Head of Post-training
traction: Prime Intellect reported more than 6,000 customers and over $100M annualized revenue in July 2026.
notes: The company-reported commercial acceleration is strong, but the surface area is unusually broad for its size and the marketplace is capital and operations intensive. Network effects and post-training workflow retention need independent validation.

name: Arize AI
product: A platform for tracing, evaluating, monitoring and troubleshooting machine-learning and generative-AI systems.
targetCustomer: Enterprise ML and generative-AI teams
buyer: VP AI, Head of ML Platform, ML Engineering Lead
traction: Arize said its open-source Phoenix project exceeded two million monthly downloads at the time of the Series C.
notes: Open-source distribution is meaningful, but observability and evaluation are crowded and risk feature absorption by model and cloud platforms. A durable moat likely requires proprietary evaluation workflows and accumulated enterprise feedback data.

name: Modular
subsector: AI compiler, runtime and programming stack
product: A heterogeneous AI compute stack spanning the MAX platform, Mojo language and inference runtime technology.
targetCustomer: AI developers, model providers, enterprises and chip vendors
buyer: CTO, VP AI Infrastructure, Compiler and Platform leaders
traction: Modular reported more than 100,000 developers, 24,000 GitHub stars and trillions of tokens served when announcing its 2025 financing.
notes: The compiler/runtime thesis has exceptional technical depth, but Qualcomm announced an agreement to acquire Modular in June 2026, so it is no longer a clean independent venture comparable. Closing status and future product independence remain unknown.

name: Groq
product: Purpose-built Language Processing Unit accelerators, compiler software and a cloud service for low-latency inference.
targetCustomer: AI developers, model providers, enterprises and sovereign compute programs
buyer: CTO, CIO, VP AI Infrastructure
traction: Groq reported 13 data centers, more than five million developers and trillions of tokens processed weekly in June 2026.
notes: The total adds the June 2026 financing to an Axios-reported cumulative amount through December 2025 and is approximate. A publicly announced December 2025 non-exclusive technology licensing agreement and subsequent strategic reset make current headcount and long-term hardware strategy difficult to compare.

name: FlexAI
product: A control plane intended to run AI workloads across heterogeneous accelerator and cloud environments.
targetCustomer: AI-native companies and enterprise AI platform teams
buyer: CTO, VP Infrastructure, Head of ML Platform
traction: No independently verifiable revenue, customer count or production-scale benchmark was found in the reviewed public sources.
notes: The heterogeneous-compute thesis is technically relevant and unusually aligned with European infrastructure needs, but commercial proof and reproducible performance evidence are weak publicly. Scope breadth is a product-execution risk.

name: Verda
product: A European GPU cloud, formerly DataCrunch, operating compute infrastructure in Finland and Iceland.
targetCustomer: European AI startups, researchers and enterprises
buyer: CTO, CIO, Head of ML Platform
fundingDisplay: $77M announced equity and debt; exact equity/debt split of Series A not disclosed
traction: The company disclosed new Nordic capacity plans but did not publish revenue, utilization or customer-count evidence in the reviewed sources.
notes: The company rebranded from DataCrunch to Verda in November 2025. Both the seed and Series A financing include debt, and the Series A split is unclear. Sovereignty and low-carbon Nordic capacity differentiate it; LinkedIn range and visible-profile counts are inconsistent.

name: Qdrant
product: An open-source vector database and managed or hybrid platform for semantic search and AI retrieval.
targetCustomer: AI developers and enterprise platform teams
buyer: Developer, Head of Data Platform, CTO
traction: Qdrant reported more than 250 million package downloads, 29,000 GitHub stars and production use by Canva, HubSpot and others in March 2026; revenue was not disclosed.
notes: Rust implementation, open-source distribution and hybrid deployment are credible advantages. Vector search is crowded and increasingly bundled, so the moat depends on retrieval quality, operational reliability and movement into higher-value retrieval workflows.

name: Inferact
product: A commercial company built by vLLM creators and maintainers to develop enterprise infrastructure and services around vLLM.
targetCustomer: Model providers, AI-native companies and enterprise inference teams
buyer: CTO, VP AI Infrastructure, ML Platform Lead
traction: vLLM had more than 60,000 GitHub stars and roughly 2,000 contributors when the financing was reported; Inferact revenue and enterprise-customer counts were not disclosed.
notes: Direct stewardship of a dominant open-source inference project creates exceptional technical distribution, but the enterprise business model is unproven. Moat durability depends on governance credibility, contribution velocity and converting adoption without alienating the ecosystem.
